newsitem.title: NORWAY: Fokus, UBN cooperation deal almost ready.
newsitem.headline: Fokus, UBN cooperation deal almost ready.

text.p: A cooperation agreement between Norway's Fokus Bank and Union Bank of Norway (UBN) will be finalised in August, daily Aftenposten said on Tuesday.
The newspaper quoted Fokus chief executive officer Bjarne Borgersen as saying the agreement did not block Fokus from merging with or being taken over by another bank.
"We have emphasized that the agreement with UBN be written in such a way that all options remain open," Borgersen told Aftenposten.
"The agreement is more or less complete and will most certainly be ready before the end of August," he said.
The managements of Fokus and UBN announced on May 7 they had started talks with the objective of establishing cooperation based on both banks continuing as independent entities.
They also said they would launch a joint cooperation in insurance with Danish insurer Codan Forsikring.
The initiative for the cooperation came from Fokus, whose board at the time was fighting a hostile takeover attempt by Sparebankgruppen, a group of 16 Norwegian savings banks.

The Norwegian Finance Ministry in March formally approved of a plan by Fokus and Codan to set up a joint life insurer. UBN's own insurance business is small and the savings bank has said it hopes to quickly be able to achieve a new position by cooperating with Fokus and Codan.
